skills.name: TypeScript
skills.blurb: JavaScript with a structural type system. The compiler catches the class of bug that otherwise turns up in production at 2am, and the types double as documentation that cannot go stale.
skills.note: Six years of it. Types catch more than my tests do.

skills.name: Node.js
skills.blurb: A JavaScript runtime on V8 with a non-blocking event loop. A good fit for services that spend most of their time waiting on other services rather than on the CPU.
skills.note: Seven years. Mostly REST services and API gateways.

skills.name: Python
skills.blurb: The default runtime for anything touching a model. With FastAPI and async it is quick enough for real services, which is where the model-facing half of my systems lives.
skills.note: FastAPI services and every AI pipeline I have shipped.

skills.name: NestJS
skills.blurb: An opinionated Node framework with real dependency injection and module boundaries. The structure still makes sense when the third engineer joins the codebase.
skills.note: DI and modules. Structure that survives a growing team.

skills.name: PostgreSQL
skills.blurb: The relational database that usually turns out to be the right answer. Transactions you can trust, JSONB while the schema is still moving, and pgvector when you need similarity search.
skills.note: My default database. JSONB and pgvector when needed.

skills.name: Redis
skills.blurb: An in-memory store used as cache, lock, rate limiter and queue. The cheapest way to take load off a database that has started to struggle under read traffic.
skills.note: Caching, locks and rate limits on the hot paths.

skills.name: RabbitMQ
skills.blurb: A message broker that decouples the request from the work behind it. Anything slow, flaky or expensive goes behind a queue, and calls out to a model are all three at once.
skills.note: Everything slow or flaky goes behind a queue.

skills.name: Docker
skills.blurb: Containers, so the same image runs on my laptop, in CI and in production. Unglamorous work, and the reason a deploy stopped being an event anyone had to watch.
skills.note: Local, CI and production running the same image.

skills.name: LLM & RAG
skills.blurb: Retrieval-augmented generation, agent orchestration, model routing and evals. The engineering around the model, which is where most of the actual work turns out to be.
skills.note: RAG, evals, and keeping answers grounded in sources.

skills.name: Google Cloud Platform
skills.blurb: Google Cloud Platform. The cloud provider I have the most experience with, and the one that has the best managed services for AI pipelines.
skills.note: Managed services for AI pipelines and production workloads.

skills.name: React
skills.blurb: A component-based frontend library. The right tool for the job when the UI is complex, and the wrong one when it is not.
skills.note: Complex UIs, and the wrong tool when they are not.

skills.name: Angular
skills.blurb: A component-based frontend framework. The right tool for the job when the UI is complex, and the wrong one when it is not.
skills.note: Complex UIs, and the wrong tool when they are not.

skills.name: Next.js
skills.blurb: A React framework with server-side rendering, static generation and API routes. The right tool for the job when the UI is complex, and the wrong one when it is not.
skills.note: Complex UIs, and the wrong tool when they are not.

skills.name: GitHub
skills.blurb: A web-based Git repository hosting service. The go-to place for version control and collaboration.
skills.note: Version control and collaboration.

skills.name: HTML
skills.blurb: The standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser. The backbone of the web.
skills.note: The backbone of the web.

skills.name: CSS
skills.blurb: A style sheet language used for describing the presentation of a document written in HTML or XML. The skin of the web.
skills.note: The skin of the web.

skills.name: JavaScript
skills.blurb: A high-level, often just-in-time compiled, and multi-paradigm programming language. The language of the web.
skills.note: The language of the web.

skills.name: GraphQL
skills.blurb: A query language for your API, and a server-side runtime for executing queries by using a type system you define for your data.
skills.note: Query language for APIs.

skills.name: Firebase
skills.blurb: A platform developed by Google for creating mobile and web applications. It provides a real-time database and backend as a service.
skills.note: Real-time database and backend as a service.

skills.name: Apache Kafka
skills.blurb: An open-source distributed event streaming platform used by thousands of companies for high-performance data pipelines, streaming analytics, data integration, and mission-critical applications.
skills.note: Distributed event streaming platform.
